newsitem.title: CHILE: Carter praises Chilean human rights record.
newsitem.headline: Carter praises Chilean human rights record.

text.p: Former U.S. President Jimmy Carter, an opponent of Chile's former military rulers, praised the country's progress on Thursday on human rights and the economy.
Carter, who arrived in Chile on Wednesday, was declared an illustrious citizen of Santiago by Mayor Jaime Ravinet and was due to meet President Eduardo Frei.
"Now the situation is very different. ... The whole world has noticed the progress Chile has made on human rights and the economy," Carter said in halting Spanish in a speech at Santiago city hall.

As president from 1977 to 1981, Carter was constantly at odds with Chile's military regime over its mistreatment of political prisoners and refusal to extradite officers accused of the 1976 murder in Washington of former Chilean foreign minister Orlando Letelier and an American aide.

Since its return to civilian rule in 1990, Chile has restored civil liberties and released political prisoners recognised by major international human rights groups. But these group are still sharply critical of brutality by Chile's Carabineros police and would like to see changes in Chile's constitution, which was dicated by then-military President Augusto Pinochet and gives the military a great deal of power.
